newsitem.title: USA: Otis Elevator revenues up 6 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Otis Elevator revenues up 6 pct in 1996.

text.p: Otis Elevator Co's had a very good year in 1996 with revenues rising 6 percent helped by the strongest North American sales in some time, President Jean-Pierre van Rooy said Tuesday.
Reporting revenues of $5.6 billion for the United Technologies Corp subsidiary, he told a media briefing "The market is not growing in Europe as good as we hoped."
In North America, 1996 was "the strongest year for use in some time," he said.
Today, he continued, Otis is doing "better in the U.S., (but) Europe is still slow."
Van Rooy said profits rose 3 percent in 1996 to $524 million. He noted profits would have been up 6 percent, and revenues 9 percent, at constant foreign exchange rates.
He said "1996 was not nearly so kind to some of our competitors," noting Otis is "one and a half times the size of our next largest competitior, the Swiss-based Schindler Holding AG.
"We have seen dramatic growth of Pacific Asia in recent years and anticipate a doubling of this market, excluding Japan, over the next decade," van Rooy said.
He said the area now accounts for $1.6 billion of the company's revenues, or nearly 30 percent of the total.
"We are confident about the future," van Rooy said, "because accelerated urbanization throughout Asia will continue to increase demand for our products."
